utterances.text: Therefore you answered using an assumption. Do you have a very clear and exact memory of the Ogrjev building in 1993, that is to say in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I think -- well, precisely, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember then, outside of the main entrance that we have seen abundantly on the film and also in the photograph, another door which gave direct access to the road?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I do not remember having seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Would the usher please show the witness very quickly Document 245, Prosecution Exhibit 245.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this photograph was taken on the 16th of April, 1993, by a British officer. Do you recognise what is seen here in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the fence for the Ogrjev facility on the right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on this fence, indeed in the beginning part of this fence, a gate which is closed in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I do here. Here (indicating). You're referring to this; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this gate which you've just pointed out for us, does that still exist today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are we therefore to conclude then that the premises have been modified? Are we in agreement with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: This part, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, have you ever gone into the house of Mr. Anto Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, how were you able to give us your point of view about what was located within that house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I did not say that I was talking about that -- oh, yes, Anto Papic. Oh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I thought that you were referring to Drago Josipovic. Anto Papic; is that the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Anto Papic, that's right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I did go to his home, yes. I did go to his home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what reason did you go to Mr. Anto Papic's home?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: He came to see us because of our children who were playing on his lawn and they messed up his grass, and he wanted us to come and see this for ourselves and to tell our children not to do that because our children only made fun of him and didn't take what he said seriously, so then we really went to see his place and we had a cup of coffee with him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. At that time, were you living close to the house of Mr. Anto Papic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No. I lived in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would go to Ahmici, is that right, with your children?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No, no. No, I didn't have to go to Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I wish to try to understand. You stated, if I understand correctly, according to the transcript, that your children allegedly damaged the lawn of Mr. Anto Papic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No. It was children from his neighbourhood. There is this Lasva River where they go to swim and then they go out and they play ball on his lawn, and then we would come to caution these children to not to do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Generally speaking then, before the month of April 1993, would you often go either for personal reasons or in your professional capacity to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No, not very often, no, not to the village of Ahmici. I would pass through Ahmici along the main road, but I didn't really ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regards to the lawn that was somewhat damaged, are you saying that the police would go to Ahmici for something like that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes. The policemen who worked on the ground. Then they went to Ahmici, Nadioci, Poculica, Kruscica, Krcevine, et cetera, and then we'd come by and tell them what not to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question I'm asking you: In the circumstances at that time, would incidents as minor as children walking on someone's lawn justify sending out the police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Our police had people who used to work out on the ground, and they would patrol villages and receive reports and resolve these matters on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this was not your case. You were a technician, a criminology technician. You were not a specialist in lawns being stepped on or played on by children.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No, but as soon as I finished school in '80, '81, '82, I worked in that area with these other policemen, and we would pass by and tell people what they were not supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know the accused Vlado Santic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain to this Trial Chamber under what circumstances you came to know him and what relations you had with him, personal relations or professional relations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I met Vlado Santic when I started working at the police station. Actually, I met him before that, when I was supposed to go to school. He brought me the news that I had been admitted into this school. When I finished this school, I started working in Vitez, and I have known him ever since and we were friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please explain more in detail about the time period of interest; that is to say, April 1992 to, let's say, April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: In '92, Vlado Santic worked in the crime investigation police, and then he was transferred to, I think, the military police, so we didn't work together anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please specify the dates on which Vlado Santic was sent to work in the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: The date? I could not really specify it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you specify the time period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Perhaps mid '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're stating then that after mid 1992, you no longer had any contact with Vlado Santic due to the fact that he went to join the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: We did not have any professional cooperation, but we would see each other every now and then and have a drink perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. But before that, did you have close relations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes. But life is so fast, so very busy, and with all these events unravelling, there wasn't much time for socialising.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. I would like now to turn to the question of the composition of the police department in Vitez in which you yourself worked. You stated that the chief of this department was Pero Skopljak, at least at the time at which you entered into service in 1992, in April. What was Pero Skopljak's professional background?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I only know that in '91, when the elections were held, that he was appointed by the political party that he represented, and I don't know about his background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a person that was trained to administer the police and trained in police techniques?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: He had a university degree, but I don't know about police work. Usually political persons were appointed to these posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Pero Skopljak was appointed to this post at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, you would say this was a political appointment which would not be justified by any professional specialties or special expertise in this particular area; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: That's the way it was in practice before, and it was inherited that way too, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Was Pero Skopljak and Mr. Vlado Santic, did the two men have any close relations, personal relations, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you talked about the police reserves, that is to say, police positions made up of reservists and who were sent into various local communities surrounding Vitez, and you stated that one of these police stations made up of reservists was stationed in Ahmici, Santici, and Nadioci, and this was led by Zaid Ahmic. Would you please tell us whether these local police forces made up of police reserves were ethnically balanced?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. In local communities, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this ethnic balance representative of the ethnic composition of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Usually an effort was made to have it half-half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Consequently, when the reserve posts for Ahmici were mentioned, including Santici, we are to understand that the reserve police force was made up of Muslims and of Croats?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, we are to understand that when weapons were distributed to these police reservists, they were sent both to Croats and to Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed that after the month of October 1992, at the end of October 1992, that the Croatian authorities asked for the Muslim members in the areas of Ahmici, Santici, and another part of that area to submit or surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let us talk now about the ethnic balance within the professional police force within Vitez.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you stated that this balance was maintained up until October 1992 and that after October 1992 that the Muslims, or many Muslims who made up the police force in Vitez, went or split off to form another group in Mahala. You also stated that in 1992, a certain person named Arko Kraljevic [as interpreted] entered into the police station in Vitez and disarmed a number of Muslim police officers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't recall that. I wasn't there. I don't remember him disarming these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I need to correct the transcript which does not reflect faithfully the question I just put to you. With your permission, Witness, I would like to ask you once again: Do you remember this event which took place in June 1992 and do you recall that Darko Kraljevic and several other persons from the HVO entered into this police station and disarmed the Muslim policemen located there and then finally kicked them out of this police station, of course? Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't remember that event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know Mr. Darko Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please explain exactly who this person is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: He is a member of the special purposes unit formed by the HOS and the Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall that following a number of incidents, including the one I have just mentioned and which you do not recall, that relations between the Croat policemen and Muslim policemen gradually deteriorated during the summer of 1992 and the fall of 1992 to such an extent that a split occurred during the month of October? In your opinion, if this doesn't correspond to your own memory, what were the causes of this deep splintering between the Croatian and Muslim policemen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Before the Muslims and Croats separated, in the police station it was said that HDZ, SDA, that is to say the political parties, which political party would win, which would lead, and so those were the types of discussions that were going on at the police station at that time and the differences of view was with relation to political issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that in October 1992, Pero Skopljak was replaced by Mirko Samija, the name that you mentioned a moment ago, Mr. Samija, and that the new head of police in Vitez notified the Muslims that they would be subject to an investigation in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I do know that after Pero Skopljak resigned Mirko Samija replaced him, and that an investigation should come from Mostar, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned that there was a growing insecurity in Vitez and in the area of Vitez during the year of 1992 and during the early weeks of 1993. It seemed to me, but perhaps you may correct me if you feel that I'm incorrect, it seems to me that you were implying that this situation of insecurity -- rather, you were blaming this insecurity on this militia army such as the HOS and the Vitezovi and perhaps the Jokeri. Have I correctly interpreted your statements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your own opinion, did these armed militias pursue different objectives than that of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't know what their objectives were. All I know is that we, as the civilian police, were able to do nothing because if a uniformed young man showed that he belonged to some kind of unit, then he would do what he liked and we weren't able to go about our duties, but I don't know what the political objectives were or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this regard, with regard to your own duties to respond as a civilian police officer, would it make a difference whether someone belonged to one of the militias, such as the Jokeri or the HOS, or whether they belonged to another unit, such as a regular unit, if you will, of the HVO, such as those coming from the Vitez Brigade? Would there be a difference for you whether they were a member of the HVO or a member of the militia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Well, there was a difference, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please specify what that difference would be?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: The paramilitary ones would usually wear black uniforms. They would have very short haircuts, practically no hair at all. Individuals who were members of these units would get drunk, they were prone to carousing, and they would disturb law and order generally, whereas the ones in the brigade, they were okay men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please remind me -- I know you've already spoken of this, but I think this is important enough for me to repeat this question. Could you remind me of which authority was in place and had command of the HOS, the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: In Vitez, the HOS was an independent, autonomous unit, and what they decided to do, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There must have been a leader or a commander. I think you mentioned it a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: The chief of the Vitezovi was Darko Kraljevic in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether or not they had any Jokers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I heard about the Jokers, that they were stationed in Nadioci and that they belonged to a military police unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the chain of command under which they were located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know? You know it for the HOS but not for the Jokers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: They were more isolated and didn't cause as many problems as HOS. I only knew of their name. I had just heard of them by name, but I didn't actually know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't any of the officers at that time, none of the persons in charge at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Now I would like to request that the usher show to the witness document 343, Exhibit 343.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm showing this document to you now simply in order to perhaps call your attention to the heading and to see to whom this order was addressed, and you see here that it is signed by Colonel Blaskic. You may also note that among the persons to whom this is addressed you'll find the Vitezovi formation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I can see that it says "Vitezovi."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then could we not conclude, sir, that the forces within the Vitezovi, whom you've described in such a poor light as having had very poor behaviour and acting as drunks, that these people, indeed, were in the chain of command that went down from Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I just know that they worked, as I said beforehand, but as to these structures, I wasn't informed of that. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you will also note that among the people to whom this order from Colonel Blaskic was addressed, you will also find the 4th Battalion of the military police in Vitez. Who was the head of this military police in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I think that for the 4th Battalion, the commander was -- just a moment. I think it was Ivan Budimir, the 4th Battalion Military Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in a document which was submitted a moment ago and tendered as evidence which is listed as D30/2, it is stated here that an incident occurred which you described in great detail and which was attributed to one person in particular from the Vitezovi. The author of this document who described this event, this incident, says that this incident is deplorable in that it gives the impression that the HVO forces are divided. I'm now referring to the last paragraph of this document. It is signed Pasko Ljubicic and Miso Mijic. Isn't this a sign, if not proof, of the fact that the militia, who we've just described and who behaved so poorly, these militias who were responsible for this feeling of insecurity in the area are, indeed, within the chain of command of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I really don't know that. All I know is that it was rumoured and discussed, talked about, that all the units should be placed under one cap, so to speak, but as far as I know, all the special purposes units refused to come under any umbrella, military or otherwise, or any command or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to now turn to another subject, and I'd like to talk about your own professional practices. You stated during the course of your testimony that -- rather, you gave the impression that you acted in a perfectly objective manner and that you would investigate any crime that was reported to you, regardless of whether or not this crime was attributable to Croats or to Muslims. I'd like to examine this further. First of all, I would like for you to specify what your professional relations were with the military police. In particular, I'm talking about you now as a civilian police officer. What was your power or competence in relation to the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Well, our competence was that if a military man took part in a crime, then we should turn him over to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nonetheless, it seems that when a crime was reported to you, it was your duty, nonetheless, to carry out an investigation of this crime?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: We should have -- it was up to us to carry out an investigation, but if it was a member of the military, then the military police would take over the case, and we would refer the case to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Couldn't it be imagined, perhaps, that the military police itself could have committed a crime [as translated]? In other words, if you allow me to specify or to elaborate more, you're saying that it was only when a military person or a soldier was identified as having been the perpetrator of a crime that you would then turn this person over to the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you mentioned a murder that took place ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that the interpreters are informing me now that there has been in the transcript an error. I, of course, did not state, this is at 16:20, that the military police could have committed a crime. I did not say that. I would not have even thought of such a thing. What I wanted to say was that the military police would have taken into their own hands the investigation of such a crime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, a moment ago you mentioned the killing of Samir Trako in Vitez in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was an investigation conducted in which you participated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I did not take part in that investigation, but my colleagues did, and this investigation was conducted by the investigating judge from Travnik, I think it was. I don't know what actually happened, but I do recall that there was a murder in the hotel. I wasn't on duty at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the victim a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time in May 1992, at the time of the murder of this Muslim, Samir Trako, was the Hotel Vitez occupied by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: The military police was there, but I don't know as of what date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The perpetrator of this crime, who was identified according to the report which was submitted to the Tribunal under D79/2, has been a person named Vukadinovic Perica and as having been a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that the commission which went out to investigate determined whether he was a member or not. I am not aware of that. I don't know if he was or wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Consequently, you don't know whether or not he was a member of the military police of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, this person who was identified as the perpetrator of this crime, was that person arrested?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was not arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, here we're at the end of May 1992. At that time, who was the chief of police in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Well, there were two police forces, the regional police force and the military police force. I don't know whether the 4th Battalion or -- I don't know exactly who that was. There were three types of police: The battalion, the municipal, and a regional one, and they all had their commanders. I think Ivan Budimir was, perhaps, the chief of the battalion one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall an incident that took place in November 1992 on the road from Vitez to Kruscica? This was the murder of two members of the Bosnian army, Huso Hadzic and Sead Ahem (phoen), and the third person was seriously wounded, Minet Akeljic. These three men were leaving a cafe when they were attacked. Do you recall this event?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an investigation of the circumstances of this double assassination and this attempted assassination?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I think so, yes. An investigation was carried out, I think, but I don't know. Usually, in a case of homicide, there would be an investigating judge there too, and a report would be filed, a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Vitez police involved in this investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Partly, yes, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, did this investigation lead to an arrest?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the disappearance in December 1992 of a man named Armin Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I do not remember that someone disappeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this name remind you or do you recall hearing this name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that? What was the name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Armin Arnautovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: "Arnautovic" is a well-known surname. Yes, "Arnautovic" is a surname that exists in Vitez, but the first name ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a memory of a supposed accident that occurred where someone allegedly was killed in an area called Zume?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not recall, then, having been personally in charge of an investigation, of this investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Possibly, but right at this very moment, I cannot remember this accident. There were many accidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall -- and I hope that you recall this -- an explosive attack against a Muslim store in Vitez in December 1992? I have here before me the name of some of the victims. I do not believe you will contest the fact that this attack took place, but my question is as follows: Did you carry out or conduct any investigation, and did these investigations lead to any arrests?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I didn't really understand this. Do we know who the perpetrator was? Is that your question?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No, sir, the question was as follows: In December, 1992, for example, in particular on the 24th and 25th and 26th of December 1992, several Muslim stores in Vitez were destroyed by explosive weapons. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I recall that. I remember that explosives were thrown at Muslim cafes and shops. That, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these attacks lead to an investigation, and did these investigations allow you to arrest the perpetrators of these attacks?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: This was the subject of an investigation, but the perpetrators were not discovered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to now turn to the murder of Mr. Esada Salkic in February 1993 in Nadioci. You stated now that you carried out an investigation, and I see here that you were able to carry out the identification of the person who was assassinated, or murdered, and that you also [interpretation interrupted] to the Kaonik prison. Could you please tell us, who was Miroslav Bralo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Until that moment, I never knew Miroslav Bralo. After that event, I got to know this person better. During the war, I had heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrested him, was he a civilian, or military? Or a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: At that time, he was a civilian. He was in that capacity. And then in the police station, this was discussed, whether he belonged to someone or not. And he said that he was a member of the Vitezovi. And then when we checked with the Vitezovi, they said no, that he was not their member. So that is why we continued to work on that case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Miroslav Bralo ever brought to trial or arrested, rather, for his murder of Esada Salkic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: He was delivered to the Kaonik prison, and proceedings were supposed to be initiated against him. But I do not know whether further proceedings were initiated or whether this was fully carried out. I don't know for sure. I just know that we started this, but how far it went, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you just stated that you learned a great deal about Miroslav Bralo during the war, but you did not know whether or not he had been tried or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I was not interested in it later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you weren't informed that he left prison very quickly thereafter?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: We heard about it. I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you knew that he had not been tried?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether he was sentenced, but I don't know that he got out quickly. I don't know how or why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you not know who gave the order releasing him from prison?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Miroslav Bralo did after he was released from prison?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I know that he joined the Vitezovi, I think, because I saw him armed later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have another question, and then I think I will have finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated, sir, that Counsellor Glumac submitted a number of reports to this Tribunal, reports of investigations, and these reports were described or stamped "Military Secret" and were carried out in the course of investigation. I'd like to know whether or not, to your knowledge, there exists a report of this type on the events which took place on the 16th of April, 1993, in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't know of the existence of any report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, as a policeman, and as a specialist in criminal investigations, were you not interested in what had occurred in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: The war was on then, and at first I didn't even know what had happened in Ahmici. And perhaps only three or four days later, I heard that the U.N. found some persons who had burned down in a house. And this -- this shook me. I mean, how could these people have burned? And some ten days or so later, there was some kind of an exchange, and I heard that in Ahmici they found 50 or 60 victims and there would be an exchange. But before that, I didn't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ahmici was in your precinct, was it not? So you would have been in charge of carrying out an investigation. If you were sent to carry out an investigation about Mr. Pavelic's grass, then a crime in Ahmici would have been within your scope of responsibility, would it have not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: The war started on the 16th, and then it was impossible to go out into the field and carry out investigations. There were frontlines, people went to defence lines, and we practically stopped operating as a crime investigations police. I only worked as a criminology technician in terms of identifying the corpses that were found in town; and also if there was a burglary or something, then I would interview people to see what was going on. But in the surrounding villages, where the lines were, that is where we couldn't go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your opinion as a technician, as a criminal technician, does a war involve the murder of 128 civilian women and children? Is that truly war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think that's a matter for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Withdraw the question, Mr. President. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Glumac, it's now half past 4.00; are you going to be many minutes in reexamination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No, I'll be short.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, how much time do we have? 15 minutes? Would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask the interpreters. Are they all right for another quarter of an hour? I think everybody else is. THE INTERPRETERS: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: They say yes. But no more.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. Strukar, could you please tell the Court, is there a place for a photograph in your employment booklet?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: As far as I can remember the employment booklet, no, there was no place for a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the usher to show this employment book to the witness and to the Court and to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: This is the originals, and you tell me whether that was the book that was photocopied, and tell me whether the data entered in this book are the data on the basis of which you obtained your pension, on the basis of which you retired, and whether the data also have a registry number, and whether they can be checked.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes, this is the original. Yes, I know by the stamp and by the handwriting up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Could the usher please show this to the Trial Chamber. This is the original. And also to the Prosecutor, please. If the Prosecutor is contesting the authenticity of this document, we can also find the document on the basis of which all these entries were made, if that is the case. I think that the Prosecutor can object if they don't want this to be admitted into evidence, or if he contests it in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't expect there is any dispute about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have not made an objection to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's question, to Mr. Terrier's question, you said that Pero Skopljak was appointed in a way as a political person; not as a professional in the force, but as a person who was involved in political work?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: And this post of chief of police, in the previous system, was it always a political post?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: It was a political post, and it was -- and also this other post of commander was always a political post too. And there was only one term of office, I think, of two years or four years, I'm not sure, and then the structure would change again. Sometimes it would be a Muslim, sometimes it would be a Croat, depending on ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this was after the elections, do you know whether Pero Skopljak was appointed by consensus between the HDZ and the SDA? That is to say whether he was accepted both by the Croats and the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Also could you please tell me -- tell the Court, this other post of the commander of the police, and you said that that was second in importance, was that post also one that could be obtained only by consensus? That is to say, did they have to reach agreement on that too?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes, agreement had to be reached on that point too, and the commander also was not a professional in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Also the Prosecutor asked you about the attack on the police station in June 1992, and you said that you did not remember. However, do you remember whether in June and all the way up to October policemen of Muslim ethnic background worked at the police station in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They worked together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Were there any interruptions in their work before the 19th of October, 1992, when the Muslim policemen definitely left?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. No, no, there were no interruptions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Also I would like to ask you to tell the Court about the request that was put forth that Pero Skopljak and his deputy, I think Saban Mahmutovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: That they should both leave the police station. Was this the joint agreement reached by the Croats and the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The Muslims put forth the following condition, that Pero Skopljak should resign, and the Croats said that Commander Saban Mahmutovic should resign, and they were from these political parties of theirs, and they were the most responsible for their behaviour in town, and Pero Skopljak did resign, whereas Saban would not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Did anybody from the civilian authorities or from your immediate superiors in the police, did any one of these persons ever tell you not to do your work, not to carry out investigations, not to receive reports, not to perform regular police duties?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No, no. No one ever ordered that nor did anyone ever say that or anything. We worked as much as we could, it was difficult for us, but we did whatever we could. We gathered evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: In your work, did you have a different treatment towards a situation when the victim was a Croat and different when the victim was a Muslim? Did you make any distinction between the two?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: As far as I know, we made no distinctions. We would always go out to investigate, to collect evidence and information and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor also asked you whether you know anything connected to the circumstances of Miroslav Bralo, Cicko's, release from prison. You said you didn't.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I don't know who let him out or why. I know that I heard it bandied about town, that they said Cicko's free and that he was in a unit of some kind, that he joined some kind of military unit, I think the Vitezovi, but I'm not sure, because our hands were tied.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Tell us another thing, please, and that's the last question in connection with the events in Ahmici, whether the civilian police could, in any way whatsoever, conduct an investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: At that time, it could not because it was under the domain of the army, the line was there, and it had no competencies whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Who did have the competence in case of an investigation being conducted? Who could have carried out this investigation? Could this have been done by the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: No. I think it was only the military police who could have done that because they were uniformed individuals, and so it was only the military police who could have conducted an investigation of this kind. We could not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the military police did launch an investigation of any kind or whether a request was made to ascertain what had, in fact, happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STRUKAR
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for coming, Mr. Strukar. You are released now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
